metadata.title: A call to action: a systematic review of ethical and regulatory issues in using process data in educational assessment

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study is a desk-based systematic literature review and does not analyze a student-level large-scale assessment dataset. Because no primary microdata are used, there is no sampling frame, no complex survey design, and no application of student or replicate weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT or BRR/jackknife). The review instead codes and summarizes characteristics of 22 eligible publications using an ordinal coding scheme aligned to Sclater’s (2016) code of practice. Therefore, weighting guidance for ILSA plausible values or survey inference is not applicable to the empirical unit of analysis (the included studies).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) are generated for cognitive achievement scales in ILSA assessments, but this paper does not estimate student achievement scores from ILSA microdata. Instead, it synthesizes published studies and codes whether ethical/privacy/regulatory elements are present using an ordinal rubric. Missing-data handling for PVs or student responses is therefore not part of the methodology because there is no student-level dataset being imputed or deleted.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Systematic review selection: searches (2010–2018) in ERIC, Web of Science, and ProQuest plus hand-searching six journals and conference/special issue proceedings; inclusion required English-language refereed conference/report/book/paper, a K-12 educational context, reference to assessment/test outcomes, and reference to process/log/user-generated data plus ethical/regulatory issues. When only three K-12 studies met the key inclusion criteria, the authors applied second-order eligibility criteria to include studies in education contexts (K-12, higher education, training/adult) that referenced learning/process data and assessment and also mentioned ethical/regulatory issues. Final eligible set comprised 22 studies for full-text screening and coding.

main_findings.dataset_used: ILSA literature synthesis (systematic review; no single student-level analytic micro-dataset)

The authors searched multiple databases and hand-searched journals for 2010–2018, initially finding 1349 records after deduplication and screening down to 66 full-text candidates, then to 22 eligible studies after applying first- and second-order eligibility criteria. They coded each included study using a modified Sclater (2016) code of practice with eight categories (e.g., Responsibility, Transparency & consent, Privacy, Validity, Access, Stewardship of data, Enabling positive interventions, Minimising adverse impact) on a 0–3 ordinal scale, then summarized medians/ranges and subgroup differences. Across the 22 studies, ethics-related issues were found to feature minimally overall, with comparatively higher attention to Privacy and Transparency & consent, while responsibility and stewardship of data were rarely addressed. data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction yields no student-level ML outputs because the article is a systematic review that synthesizes previously published studies rather than training predictive models on ILSA/LSA microdata. Consequently, there is no assessment cycle, grade/domain achievement outcome, PV handling, or missing-data strategy for student responses to extract. The main empirical evidence is the coded presence/absence and depth of ethical/privacy/regulatory elements across 22 included publications, summarized with descriptive statistics (medians/ranges) rather than predictive performance metrics.
